data.name: Marmaduke
data.gender_notes: Marmaduke is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old English words 'marm' (sea) and 'duc' (ruler), Marmaduke was a popular name for brave knights in medieval England. In Christian lore, Marmaduke is also associated with St. Marmaduke, a 13th-century Scottish saint. The name Marmaduke carries the meaning “Mighty warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Marmaduke usually hope their child will grow to embody mighty warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of courage and strength, Marmaduke is a reminder to face life's challenges with unwavering faith.
data.etymology: Marmaduke belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mighty warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marmaduke total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Marmaduke is an interesting name that carries a rich cultural heritage, originating from the Old English words 'marm' (sea) and 'duc' (ruler). In medieval England, this name was given to brave knights, reflecting their strength and power over the sea. It also suggests a connection to the coastal regions and the maritime community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian lore, Marmaduke is also associated with St. Marmaduke, a 13th-century Scottish saint who is said to have given his life in defense of the faith. The name carries spiritual significance as a reminder of courage, devotion, and resistance in the face of adversity. St. Marmaduke's life story can inspire us to be strong in our beliefs and unwavering in our commitment to God, even in the midst of difficult circumstances.
